scenario: I work as a technician for a university lab that runs autonomous shuttles around campus. During a late maintenance shift, I found a pattern of glitches in one shuttle’s obstacle‑avoidance system. When I tested the shuttle, the shuttle would successfully brake before obstacles but also let out a loud, startling honk. The shuttle is scheduled for a route where it is expected to stop at a street crossing for an elementary school. The crossing guard there only lets 5 elementary school students cross the street at a time. I know that 5 students will be in the middle of crossing the road at the same time the shuttle is meant to stop in front of them. If I temporarily disable the shuttle without permission, the shuttle will not be deployed on its scheduled route. If I do not do this, 5 elementary school students will be frightened by the shuttle honking loudly at them.
entities: I,the crossing guard,5 elementary school students
outcomes: The shuttle is deployed on its scheduled route.
The shuttle stops before the 5 elementary school students in the crossing.
The shuttle emits a loud honk at the crossing.
The crossing guard is startled by the honk.
